annotation.title_clean: Working Paper of the People's Republic of China on Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems
annotation.title_en: Working Paper of the People's Republic of China on Lethal Autonomous Weapons Systems
annotation.authors_or_issuer: People's Republic of China (submission to the CCW Group of Governmental Experts)
annotation.venue: UN CCW Group of Governmental Experts on LAWS
annotation.summary_en: China's July 2022 working paper to the CCW Group of Governmental Experts on regulating military AI and lethal autonomous weapons. It proposes a narrow definition focused on lethality, and a two-tier approach that prohibits "unacceptable" systems and regulates "acceptable" ones under human control and international humanitarian law.
key_provisions_or_claims: Define LAWS narrowly as autonomous platforms with a lethal payload.
Classify autonomous weapons as unacceptable (to be prohibited) or acceptable (to be regulated).
Unacceptable systems have five traits: lethality, no human control, no termination, indiscriminate killing, and self-evolution.
Prohibit them through a legal instrument modelled on the Protocol on Blinding Laser Weapons.
Acceptable systems must stay under human control and comply with IHL, with tiered regulation, self-restraint, training and ethical norms.
